label: GO step: committing to a1 after a rewarded (non-rare) trial, early/mid episode
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never D1/D2), when the previous trial was rewarded and the agent picks a1 (policy argmax a1; 99.9% of mass on action a1, choice logit mostly > 8). It is essentially silent when the rewarded previous trial was a rare transition (prev_common==0: 628 of 74k activations), so it marks the model-based stay-with-a1 case after common-rewarded trials (prev_common -1 = window start, included). It also turns off late in the episode: rate falls from ~9% of steps before trial 60 to ~0 after trial 80, so an ep_trial < 75 cutoff is part of the predicate. Magnitude tends to grow over a streak of consecutive rewarded a1 GO steps and is low in the first rewarded trial after an unrewarded or rare one. Never fires for a2 choices, unrewarded previous trials, or penalties. Recorded with model_act (the agent own computed choice) instead of the future action variable; the action==1 version scores the same (dev F1 0.935 vs 0.935).

issues: The ep_trial<75 cutoff is a hard threshold standing in for a gradual decline. Precision is 0.957 for ep_trial<60, 0.72 for 60-74 and 0.07 for >=75 (dev). 'Early/mid episode' describes it fairly, but the boundary is approximate.

There is a small precision drop on the first rewarded trial after an unrewarded one (two trials back prev_reward==0): test precision 0.76, with low mass (recall 0.18 but mass 0.096). This fits the explanation's claim about magnitude building up, so it is not an unexplained class.

start_high, good, value and choice>8 do not replace the ep_trial cutoff. With good==2 & a1 after reward, precision is still 0.85, so the feature is driven by the agent's choice, not by the hidden good state.

The other claims check out on dev. Never active off GO (precision 0 on D1/D2). Never active after an unrewarded or penalty trial (0 active). Almost never active on a2 (mass 4e-5). prev_common==0 holds 0.2% of mass. Test F1 is 0.934, matching the report.
